blocks.title: Balanced tree
blocks.text: A balanced tree keeps its height as small as possible: the heights of the left and right subtrees of any node differ by no more than a set amount, commonly 1. This keeps searching, insertion and deletion close to O(log n).

A library could organize books by category: the root is Science, its children Physics and Biology, then Physics into Classical Mechanics and Quantum Physics and Biology into Botany and Zoology, with no branch much longer than the others. Finding Quantum Physics means going Science, then Physics, then Quantum Physics; because the height stays logarithmic in the number of categories, the search is quick.
